column1: # boru Language Specification: module fn-VALUE application boundary
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Boundary rows for a module-captured Function VALUE applied inside its
# own module — the execFnDefSig same-registry dispatch class routed onto
# the main-tape frame splice (design/legacy/SUB-ENGINE-MAIN-TAPE-REVIEW.0.ignore R2)
# — and for the ARGUMENTS-ARE-INERT invariant
# (design/legacy/ARG-SEMANTICS-UNIFICATION.0.ignore): an argument never acts on its
# own; binding style (named vs unnamed) changes only how the body refers
# to it. The callee here is an ANONYMOUS fn in the export map (a named
# module fn resolves through its registered body-runner handler instead)
# and the caller takes it via an UNNAMED Function param, so the raw value
# sits on the body frame — the exact shape that used to auto-fire on
# placement.
# Go twins (value-result pins, args-stack balance, the cross-registry
# negative, and the flow-unwind leak pins) live in
# lang/go/native/fnvalue_sameregistry_test.go and
# lang/go/native/args_inert_test.go.
# §1  arguments are inert — placement alone does nothing
import module [def useanon fn [[Function Integer] [Integer] [args.1]] export "L" {useanon: useanon/v, mk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul 3]])}] end L.useanon L.mk 14
column3: an unnamed fn-value arg does NOT fire on frame placement — the body returns the sibling Integer untouched (42/126 would mean the fn fired); the unconsumed fn value is discarded by the return discipline

column1: import module [def keep fn [[Function] [Function] [args.0]] export "L" {keep: keep/v, mk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul 3]])}] end typeof (L.keep L.mk)
column3: an unnamed fn-value arg is real data — readable via args.N and returnable, exactly like a named binding read via /v

column1: import module [def useanon fn [[Function Integer] [Integer] [(args.0 args.1)]] export "L" {useanon: useanon/v, mk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul 3]])}] end L.useanon L.mk 14
column3: explicit application via args.N fires EXACTLY once — no double dispatch from placement plus body

column1: # §2  the frame tears down — nothing leaks
import module [def useanon fn [[Function Integer] [Integer] [(args.0 args.1)]] export "L" {useanon: useanon/v, lk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def tmpz 7 x add tmpz]])}] end L.useanon L.lk 1 end tmpz
column3: a body-local def in the value-dispatched callee is torn down by the frame tail — it must NOT leak past the call

column1: # §3  errors and flow control behave exactly as named dispatch
import module [def useanon fn [[Function Integer] [Integer] [(args.0 args.1)]] export "L" {useanon: useanon/v, bm: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [raise oops_e "bang"]])}] end L.useanon L.bm 1
column3: a raise inside the value-dispatched body propagates out as the same error

column1: import module [def looper fn [[Function] [Integer] [def acc 0 for 5 [def acc (acc add 1) (args.0 1)] acc]] export "L" {looper: looper/v, brk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Any] [break]])}] end L.looper L.brk
column3: a break in a value-dispatched body terminates the enclosing loop — identical to a named call (the escaped frame's cleanup tail is unwound, not leaked)

column1: import module [def looper fn [[Function] [Integer] [def acc 0 for 5 [(args.0 1) def acc (acc add 1)] acc]] export "L" {looper: looper/v, skp: (fn [[x:Integer] [Any] [continue]])}] end L.looper L.skp
column3: a continue in a value-dispatched body skips the rest of the iteration — identical to a named call; the escaped frame's args list is popped, so the caller's args stay its own

column1: # §4  a fn VALUE carries its DEFINING module's scope
# design/FUNCTION-VALUE-SCOPE.0.md. A function value's free words resolve
# in the module that WROTE it, at CALL time — not in whichever module
# happens to run it. Each row below binds the module's private helper name
# to a DIFFERENT definition at top level; the module's answer (6, or
# [3 4]) proves the body read its own, and the caller's answer (500, or an
# empty list) is the pre-fix result. Nothing type-checks the difference —
# both definitions are [[Integer] [Integer]] — so a regression here is a
# silently wrong number, not an error.
# Applying a value and NAMING it must agree: the asymmetry ("applying a
# value keeps its scope, naming it loses it") was the defect.
import module [def secret fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] def pub fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [secret n]] export "A" {pub: pub/v}] end def secret fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 100]] A.pub 5
column3: APPLYING an export resolves its free `secret` in the DEFINING module (500 = the caller's)

column1: import module [def secret fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] def pub fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [secret n]] export "A" {pub: pub/v}] end def g A.pub def secret fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 100]] g 5
column3: BINDING an export to a name keeps its scope too — `def g A.pub` must answer exactly as `A.pub`

column1: import module [def secret fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] def pub fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [secret n]] export "A" {pub: pub/v}] end def secret fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 100]] def apply1 fn [[f:Function n:Integer] [Integer] [f n]] apply1 A.pub 5
column3: a named `f:Function` PARAMETER — the commonest way a library takes a callback — keeps the argument's scope

column1: # The NATIVE callback seam (filter's Function form) GRADUATED here 2026-08-27
# (Stage 3). It was the one row of this section the compiler could not model:
# the closure lowering declined a foreign fn value and the call ISLANDED. The
# lowering now compiles the body against the DEFINING registry with the
# CALLER's CheckState shared onto it — bindings foreign, analysis local — so
# `lim` resolves in module A and the unit still lands in the caller's program.
# Its SEMANTICS are also pinned on both engines by
# lang/go/function_value_scope_test.go ("filter Function form").

import module [def lim fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [2]] def big fn [[e:Map] [Boolean] [(e dot value) gt (lim 0)]] export "A" {big: big/v}] end def lim fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [100]] filter A.big [1 2 3 4]
column3: a cross-module predicate in a NATIVE callback slot resolves `lim` in its OWN module (2), not the caller's (100)

column1: # The negative: scope travels with the VALUE, it does not open the module.
import module [def hidden fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] def only fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [hidden n]] export "A" {only: only/v}] end hidden 5
column3: a module-private word stays private — the importer cannot reach `hidden`, only the exported value can

column1: # §5  A `/v` ON A MODULE MEMBER IS DATA WHEREVER IT IS WRITTEN (NUR212, closed
#     2026-09-25): the reach's dispatch-modifier marker is never an argument,
#     so a member whose first parameter is `Any` binds through `def` as a
#     bare `/v` word always did.
import module [def up1 fn [[value:Any] [String] ['UP']] export "M" {up1: up1/v}] end def g M.up1/v end g 1
column3: a `/v`-marked member with an Any first parameter binds as a def's forward argument

column1: import module [def up fn [[value:Any opts:Map] [String] ['UP']] export "M" {up: up/v}] end def g M.up/v end g 1 {}
import module [def up1 fn [[value:Any] [String] ['UP']] export "M" {up1: up1/v}] end 7 M.up1/v
column3: …and on its own it is data over the stack

column1: import module [def up1 fn [[value:Any] [String] ['UP']] export "M" {up1: up1/v}] end M.up1 5
